title: Popovych polynomial-congruence conjecture
statement: Let n>1 and let r be a prime not dividing n. If both (X−1)^n ≡ X^n−1 and (X+2)^n ≡ X^n+2 in (ℤ/nℤ)[X]/(X^r−1), then n is prime or n² ≡ 1 (mod r).

counterexample.description: A composite n and prime r not dividing n for which n² is not 1 modulo r but both stated cyclic polynomial congruences hold exactly.
